newsitem.title: FRANCE: Korean unions vow to continue strikes.
newsitem.headline: Korean unions vow to continue strikes.

text.p: The Korean Confederation of Trade Unions (KCTU) said on Tuesday strikes would continue if the Seoul government did not commit itself to declare controversial labour and security laws null and void.
"The plan of the KCTU is to continue for the moment the one day a week strike, which is on Wednesday this week," Yoon Young-mo, international spokesman for the KCTU, told a news conference in Paris.
Yoon added that if a statement declaring the legislation null and void was not forthcoming, there would also be a general strike on February 18.

"We are calling on the government to make a clear statement that the labour and security laws are null and void," Yoon, who was due later to attend an OECD committee review of Korean labour law, told reporters.
Referring to President Kim Young-sam's earlier concession on reconsidering the laws, he added: "We believe the decision of the Korean government is unsatisfactory and does not respond to our demand.

"We will continue to demand that these laws, passed in a secret meeting, be declared null and void," he said. He added his views were shared by representatives of other Korean trade unions present in Paris for the meeting of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development.
